acip: 'PHAGS PA BRGYAD PA DANG, CHAGS BRAL SNGON SONG GI ZHUGS PA DBANG PO RDUL RNO GNYIS DANG, DE'I 'BRAS GNAS GNYIS DANG, LHA DANG MI'I RIGS NAS RIGS SKYE GNYIS DANG, TSE GCIG BAR CHAD GCIG PA DANG, PHYIR MI 'ONG BAR 'DA' BA DANG, SKYES TZAM NYID NAS 'DA' BA DANG, 'DU BYED DANG BCAS TE 'DA' BA DANG, 'DU BYED MED PAR 'DA' BA DANG, 'PHAR BA GSUM DANG, SRID RTZE'I MTHAR THUG 'GRO DANG, GZUGS MED NYER 'GRO DANG, MTHONG CHOS ZHI DANG, LUS MNGON BYED DANG, BSE RU LTA BU STE DGE 'DUN NYI SHU,
english: Here then are the twenty divisions of practitioners: (1) realized beings of the eighth type; (2–3) practitioners of either dull or sharp powers, who are at the entering stage but have already eliminated desire; (4–5) the same practitioners at the stage where they are residing in the result; (6–7) the two types of beings who pass from one high state and take rebirth either among worldly gods or humans (a process called “from nobility to nobility”); (8) “single blockers,” who are kept from their goal only by a single lifetime; (9) non-returners who go beyond within the intermediate state; (10) those who go beyond from the moment they take rebirth; (11) those who go beyond as they apply themselves; (12) those who go beyond without applying themselves; (13–15) those of the three types of spiritual upgrading first; (16) those who first “go to the highest,” or the level called “Peak of Existence”; (17) those who first go to the formless realm; (18) those who experience peace as something they see in this life; (19) those who manifest in a body; and (20) those who are like a rhinoceros. Returning to Choney Lama's commentary:]
